title: Instrumentation epic journal: prefetch heuristics & microdash
content:
Purpose:
This is a working journal for the Q1 instrumentation epic that bundles: prefetch/kv-cache observability, low-cost microdash widgets for fast triage, adaptive trace sampling for prefetch and slow-paths, and a lightweight rollout plan. Aim is to reduce investigation time for cold-cache/eviction incidents and measure cost impact of prefetch heuristics without exploding telemetry costs.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Metric definitions to add/augment for prefetch and cache-warmth reasoning
- Trace annotation conventions for prefetch, evictions, and fallback model calls
- Microdash widget sketches (operator-first) and minimal query patterns
- Sampling & retention policy proposals to keep trace budget bounded
- Rollout plan: canaries, synthetic probes, and guardrails

Quick summary of goals / success criteria:
- Mean time to detect & diagnose cold-cache incidents reduced by 40% vs baseline
- Prefetch metrics enable a 10% reduction in unnecessary requests to heavier model variants
- Trace budget increase limited to <= 15% of current spend via adaptive sampling and span compaction
- Dashboard microdash provides one-click triage flows for oncall

Context / background notes (notes to self):
- Recent incident: mid-Jan spike where evictions caused 30% tail-latency increase for long-context requests; root-cause: aggressive allocator churn plus cache TTL misalignment.
- Related existing artifacts: kv-warmth-signal-onboarding checklist (exists but incomplete), probe design notes. Need to avoid duplicating dashboards that already exist.

Proposed metric set (compact definitions):
1) prefetch.attempts.count
   - description: number of prefetch attempts issued (per model, per route)
   - unit: count
   - aggregation: sum per minute per (model, route)
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - SLI use: trend + spike detector (alerts on sustained >3x baseline for 5m)

2) prefetch.success.rate
   - description: fraction of prefetch attempts that resulted in cache load and were used by subsequent requests within TTL
   - unit: ratio (0-1)
   - aggregation: rolling 5m ratio; backfill window 24h
   - instrumentation: mark prefetch spans with tag prefetch.result={hit|miss|stale}

3) kv.cache.warmth.p50/p95/p99
   - description: distribution of warmness score (0..1) measured at request arrival: fraction of tokens satisfied from cached KV vs fetched
   - unit: ratio
   - aggregation: quantiles by tenant/model/route
   - notes: warmness computed cheaply at ingress code path to avoid heavy post-processing

4) prefetch.cost.estimated_tokens_saved
   - description: estimate of tokens avoided on heavy model by serving from cache / prefetched state
   - unit: token-equivalents
   - aggregation: sum daily per customer cohort
   - caution: estimation heuristic only; used for cost-awareness, not billing

5) fallback.model.invocations.count
   - description: number of fallbacks to heavier model variants triggered due to cache miss or latency SLO fallback
   - unit: count
   - aggregation: per 5m, with tenant and rollout-tag

6) probe.synthetic.latency.first_token
   - description: synthetic probe to measure TTFB for a representative prompt set, used for canary checks
   - unit: ms
   - aggregation: p50/p95/p99

Trace annotation conventions (span design):
- Root call: span.name = inference.request, tags: tenant_id, route, model.version, request_id
- Prefetch span: span.name = prefetch.kv, tags: prefetch.strategy, prefetch.batch_size, prefetch.result, prefetch.origin=(auto|manual|probe)
- KV lookup span: span.name = kv.lookup, tags: kv.shard, kv.latency_ms, kv.hit=true/false
- Fallback decision span: span.name = routing.decision, tags: reason=(eviction|latency|capacity), fallback_model
- Compacting traces: avoid including full prompt in spans; include truncated prompt_hash and token_count. Where sensitive, redaction flag.

Sampling/retention policy (proposal):
- Default span sampling: 0.5% of all inference.request for production (baseline)
- Adaptive upsample rules: if prefetch.attempts.count spikes > 2x baseline or kv.cache.warmth.p95 drops > 0.2, increase sampling to 10% for 15min for affected tenants/models
- Prefetch-critical traces: always keep traces that include prefetch.result=miss && fallback_model!=null (high diagnostic value)
- Trace TTL tiers: 7d for high-fidelity traces (canary/rollouts), 3d for adaptive samples, 30d aggregated metrics only

Microdash widget sketches (operator-first) - minimal queries and behavior:
- Widget A: Rapid warmness snapshot
  Query: last 5m p95 kv.cache.warmth grouped by model
  Purpose: immediate view of which model cohorts are cold
  Drillflow: click model -> open trace search prefetch.result=miss AND time window
- Widget B: Prefetch attempt ratio heatmap
  Query: prefetch.attempts.count / request.count by route, last 1h
  Purpose: identify runaway prefetch storms (cost risk)
- Widget C: Cost lens (estimated tokens saved vs fallback invocations)
  Query: prefetch.cost.estimated_tokens_saved / fallback.model.invocations.count daily
  Purpose: validate benefit of heuristics; quick ROI check

Dashboard UX notes:
- Microdash pages must be read-only and load under 500ms (use pre-aggregated materialized views where possible).
- Oncall flow: top row synthetic probe health + warmness p95 -> middle row models with highest fallback rate -> bottom row recent traces (compact) and top correlated alerts
- Avoid too many cross-joins in queries; prefer time-series rollups with tenant tag filters.

Rollout plan (high-level):
1) Instrumentation: add metrics + trace tags behind feature flag (2 days)
2) Canary baseline: enable sampling & microdash for internal tenants only + synthetic probes for 24–48h (1 week)
3) External limited rollout: pick 3 low-risk customers and enable prefetch heuristics + microdash (2 weeks)
4) Gradual expansion with auto-scaling of sampling when incidents observed (monitor cost)

Experiment matrix (what we'll A/B and measure):
- Axis 1: Prefetch aggressiveness (conservative / default / aggressive)
- Axis 2: Prefetch TTL (short/medium/long)
- Axis 3: Batch sizing (1, 4, 16) for prefetch ops
- Metrics to measure per cell: fallback.model.invocations.count, kv.cache.warmth.p95, probe.synthetic.latency.first_token, prefetch.cost.estimated_tokens_saved

Operational runbook notes (short):
- If warmness p95 drops > 0.25 for > 10m: switch prefetch to conservative mode (global switch), increase sampling for 30m, run eviction-debug snapshot job
- If prefetch.attempts.count > 5x baseline and cost estimate > threshold: auto-throttle prefetch for non-critical routes and notify SRE channel

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should prefetch.result=stale be treated as success or failure for the success.rate SLI? (ops says treat as miss by default)
- How to account for multi-model fanout: if prefetched KV is used by downstream reranker rather than primary model, attribute savings correctly? Need a clear attribution convention.
- Can we derive a cheap warmness score without adding extra DB lookups? Proposed: compute at admission by comparing local KV pointers + token counts.

Immediate TODO (next actions):
- [Priya] create instrumentation PR with prefetch span + minimal metrics tags (due 2026-02-26)
- [Liam] prototype microdash widgets using pre-aggregated telemetry (due 2026-03-03)
- [Maya] define adaptive sampling thresholds and implement feature flag toggles (due 2026-02-28)
- [Noah] write synthetic probe prompts and schedule canary runs (due 2026-03-01)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; I'm trying to keep the first-pass telemetry small and cheap. Expect follow-ups for metric name normalization and dashboard materializations.
- Please comment on attribution approach and any missing span tags you need for debugging.

End journal entry.
